audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Draft, source-sensitive rendering of 2 Chronicles 25 from Hebrew; YHWH used for the Tetragram. Preserves idolatry, violence, prophetic rebuke; numeric and verse-27 witness issues need collation.

verses.restored: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Amaziah was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.

modern.text: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan; she was from Jerusalem.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ מָלַ֣ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יְהוֹעַדָּ֖ן מִירוּשָׁלָֽיִם

verses.restored: He did what was right in the sight of YHWH, but not with a whole heart.

familiar.text: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, but not with a perfect heart.

modern.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not wholeheartedly.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה רַ֕ק לֹ֖א בְּלֵבָ֥ב שָׁלֵֽם

verses.restored: When the kingdom was established for him he executed the servants who had struck down the king his father.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass, when the kingdom was established to him, that he slew his servants that had killed the king his father.

modern.text: As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his grasp, Amaziah executed the servants who had murdered his father the king.

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר חָזְקָ֥ה הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַֽיַּהֲרֹג֙ אֶת עֲבָדָ֔יו הַמַּכִּ֖ים אֶת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: But he did not put their children to death, for as it is written in the Torah, in the book of Moses, which YHWH commanded, 'Fathers shall not die for the children, nor shall children die for the fathers; every man shall die for his own sin.'

familiar.text: But he slew not their children, but did as it is written in the law in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, The fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Direct citation from Mosaic Torah; communal vengeance restrained by law.

modern.text: Yet he did not put their sons to death, but acted according to what is written in the Law, in the Book of Moses, where the LORD commanded: “Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.” Amaziah’s Victories

original.text: וְאֶת בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א הֵמִ֑ית כִּ֣י כַכָּת֣וּב בַּתּוֹרָ֡ה בְּסֵ֣פֶר מֹשֶׁה֩ אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹא יָמ֨וּתוּ אָב֤וֹת עַל בָּנִים֙ וּבָנִים֙ לֹא יָמ֣וּתוּ עַל אָב֔וֹת כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ בְּחֶטְא֖וֹ יָמֽוּתוּ

verses.restored: Moreover Amaziah gathered Judah and made them captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, according to the houses of their fathers, throughout Judah and Benjamin; he numbered them from twenty years old and upward and found three hundred thousand choice men, able to go forth to war, handling spear and shield.

familiar.text: Moreover Amaziah gathered Judah together, and made them captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, according to the houses of their fathers, throughout all Judah and Benjamin: and he numbered them from twenty years old and above, and found them three hundred thousand choice men, able to go forth to war, that could handle spear and shield.

modern.text: Then Amaziah gathered the people of Judah and assigned them according to their families to commanders of thousands and of hundreds. And he numbered those twenty years of age or older throughout Judah and Benjamin and found 300,000 chosen men able to serve in the army, bearing the spear and shield.

original.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ אֶת יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיַּֽעֲמִידֵ֣ם לְבֵית אָב֗וֹת לְשָׂרֵ֤י הָאֲלָפִים֙ וּלְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֔וֹת לְכָל יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ן וַֽיִּפְקְדֵ֗ם לְמִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וַיִּמְצָאֵ֗ם שְׁלֹשׁ מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֤לֶף בָּחוּר֙ יוֹצֵ֣א צָבָ֔א אֹחֵ֖ז רֹ֥מַח וְצִנָּֽה

verses.restored: He also hired from Israel one hundred thousand mighty men of valour for a hundred talents of silver.

familiar.text: He hired also an hundred thousand mighty men of valour out of Israel for an hundred talents of silver.

modern.text: He also hired 100,000 mighty warriors from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.

original.text: וַיִּשְׂכֹּ֣ר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵ֥אָה אֶ֛לֶף גִּבּ֥וֹר חָ֖יִל בְּמֵאָ֥ה כִכַּר כָּֽסֶף

verses.restored: But a man of God came to him and said, 'O king, let not the army of Israel go with you; for YHWH is not with Israel, namely with all the sons of Ephraim.'

familiar.text: But there came a man of God to him, saying, O king, let not the army of Israel go with thee; for the LORD is not with Israel, to wit, with all the children of Ephraim.

modern.text: But a man of God came to him and said, “O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel—not with any of the Ephraimites.

original.text: וְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים בָּ֤א אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַמֶּ֕לֶךְ אַל יָבֹ֥א עִמְּךָ֖ צְבָ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין יְהוָה֙ עִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֹּ֖ל בְּנֵ֥י אֶפְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: If you go, do it; be strong for the battle. God will make you fall before the enemy, for there is power in God to help and to cast down.

familiar.text: But if thou wilt go, do it, be strong for the battle: God shall make thee fall before the enemy: for God hath power to help, and to cast down.

modern.text: Even if you go and fight bravely in battle, God will make you stumble before the enemy, for God has power to help and power to overthrow.”

original.text: כִּ֚י אִם בֹּ֣א אַתָּ֔ה עֲשֵׂ֖ה חֲזַ֣ק לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה יַכְשִֽׁילְךָ֤ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֔ב כִּ֥י יֶשׁ כֹּ֛חַ בֵּאלֹהִ֖ים לַעְז֥וֹר וּלְהַכְשִֽׁיל

verses.restored: Amaziah said to the man of God, 'What shall we do for the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Israel?' The man of God answered, 'YHWH is able to give you much more than this.'

familiar.text: And Amaziah said to the man of God, But what shall we do for the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Israel? And the man of God answered, The LORD is able to give thee much more than this.

modern.text: Amaziah asked the man of God, “What should I do about the hundred talents I have given to the army of Israel?” And the man of God replied, “The LORD is able to give you much more than this.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּמַֽה לַּעֲשׂוֹת֙ לִמְאַ֣ת הַכִּכָּ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִגְד֣וּד יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים יֵ֚שׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לָ֥תֶת לְךָ֖ הַרְבֵּ֥ה מִזֶּֽה

verses.restored: So he sent away the army that had come to him from Ephraim to return to their place; their anger was greatly kindled against Judah, and they returned home in great anger.

familiar.text: Then Amaziah separated them, to wit, the army that was come to him out of Ephraim, to go home again: wherefore their anger was greatly kindled against Judah, and they returned home in great anger.

modern.text: So Amaziah dismissed the troops who had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home. And they were furious with Judah and returned home in great anger.

original.text: וַיַּבְדִּילֵ֣ם אֲמַצְיָ֗הוּ לְהַגְּדוּד֙ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֤א אֵלָיו֙ מֵֽאֶפְרַ֔יִם לָלֶ֖כֶת לִמְקוֹמָ֑ם וַיִּ֨חַר אַפָּ֤ם מְאֹד֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וַיָּשׁ֥וּבוּ לִמְקוֹמָ֖ם בָּחֳרִי אָֽף

verses.restored: Amaziah strengthened himself, led his people, went to the Valley of Salt, and struck ten thousand of the children of Seir.

familiar.text: And Amaziah strengthened himself, and led forth his people, and went to the valley of salt, and smote of the children of Seir ten thousand.

modern.text: Amaziah, however, summoned his strength and led his troops to the Valley of Salt, where he struck down 10,000 men of Seir,

original.text: וַאֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ הִתְחַזַּ֔ק וַיִּנְהַג֙ אֶת עַמּ֔וֹ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ גֵּ֣יא הַמֶּ֑לַח וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת בְּנֵי שֵׂעִ֖יר עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִֽים

verses.restored: And other ten thousand alive the children of Judah took captive; they brought them to the top of the rock and cast them down from the top, and all were broken.

familiar.text: And other ten thousand left alive did the children of Judah carry away captive, and brought them unto the top of the rock, and cast them down from the top of the rock, that they all were broken in pieces.

modern.text: and the army of Judah also captured 10,000 men alive. They took them to the top of a cliff and threw them down so that all were dashed to pieces.

original.text: וַעֲשֶׂ֨רֶת אֲלָפִ֜ים חַיִּ֗ים שָׁבוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיְבִיא֖וּם לְרֹ֣אשׁ הַסָּ֑לַע וַיַּשְׁלִיכ֛וּם מֵֽרֹאשׁ הַסֶּ֖לַע וְכֻלָּ֥ם נִבְקָֽעוּ

verses.restored: But the band which Amaziah had sent back raided the cities of Judah from Samaria even to Beth-horon and struck three thousand of them and took much spoil.

familiar.text: But the soldiers of the army which Amaziah sent back, that they should not go with him to battle, fell upon the cities of Judah, from Samaria even unto Bethhoron, and smote three thousand of them, and took much spoil.

modern.text: Meanwhile the troops that Amaziah had dismissed from battle raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria to Beth-horon. They struck down 3,000 people and carried off a great deal of plunder. Amaziah Rebuked for Idolatry

original.text: וּבְנֵ֣י הַגְּד֗וּד אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵשִׁ֤יב אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ מִלֶּ֤כֶת עִמּוֹ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַֽיִּפְשְׁטוּ֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה מִשֹּׁמְר֖וֹן וְעַד בֵּ֣ית חוֹר֑וֹן וַיַּכּ֤וּ מֵהֶם֙ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖זּוּ בִּזָּ֥ה רַבָּֽה

verses.restored: After Amaziah came from the slaughter of the Edomites, he brought the gods of the children of Seir and set them up to be his gods; before them he bowed down and burned incense to them.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass, after that Amaziah was come from the slaughter of the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Idolatry follows military success in the narrative; cause for prophetic rebuke.

modern.text: When Amaziah returned from the slaughter of the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the Seirites, set them up as his own gods, bowed before them, and burned sacrifices to them.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵ֨י ב֤וֹא אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵֽהַכּ֣וֹת אֶת אֲדוֹמִ֔ים וַיָּבֵ֗א אֶת אֱלֹהֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י שֵׂעִ֔יר וַיַּֽעֲמִידֵ֥ם ל֖וֹ לֵאלֹהִ֑ים וְלִפְנֵיהֶ֥ם יִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה וְלָהֶ֥ם יְקַטֵּֽר

verses.restored: YHWH's anger was kindled against Amaziah, and He sent unto him a prophet who said, 'Why have you sought after the gods of the people, which did not deliver their own people out of your hand?'

familiar.text: Wherefore the anger of the LORD was kindled against Amaziah, and he sent unto him a prophet, which said unto him, Why hast thou sought after the gods of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand?

modern.text: Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and He sent him a prophet, who said, “Why have you sought this people’s gods, which could not deliver them from your hand?”

original.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בַּאֲמַצְיָ֑הוּ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֵלָיו֙ נָבִ֔יא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ לָ֤מָּה דָרַ֨שְׁתָּ֙ אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת עַמָּ֖ם מִיָּדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: As he spoke to him the king said to the prophet, 'Are you made of the king's counsel? Cease; why should you be struck?' The prophet ceased and said, 'I know that God has counseled to destroy you, because you have done this and have not heeded my counsel.'

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as he talked with him, that the king said unto him, Art thou made of the king’s counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten? Then the prophet forbare, and said, I know that God hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this, and hast not hearkened unto my counsel.

modern.text: While he was still speaking, the king asked, “Have we made you the counselor to the king? Stop! Why be struck down?” So the prophet stopped, but he said, “I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not heeded my advice.” Jehoash Defeats Amaziah (2 Kings 14:8–14)

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בְּדַבְּר֣וֹ אֵלָ֗יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַלְיוֹעֵ֤ץ לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ נְתַנּ֔וּךָ חֲדַל לְךָ֖ לָ֣מָּה יַכּ֑וּךָ וַיֶּחְדַּ֣ל הַנָּבִ֗יא וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי יָעַ֤ץ אֱלֹהִים֙ לְהַשְׁחִיתֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּ֔את וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ לַעֲצָתִֽי

verses.restored: Then Amaziah king of Judah consulted and sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, 'Come, let us meet face to face.'

familiar.text: Then Amaziah king of Judah took advice, and sent to Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, Come, let us see one another in the face.

modern.text: Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent word to the king of Israel Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu. “Come, let us meet face to face,” he said.

original.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶל יוֹאָ֨שׁ בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֧ז בֶּן יֵה֛וּא מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לך נִתְרָאֶ֥ה פָנִֽים

verses.restored: Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, 'The thistle that was in Lebanon said to the cedar of Lebanon, “Give your daughter to my son for a wife”; and a wild beast that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.'

familiar.text: And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that was in Lebanon, and trode down the thistle.

modern.text: But Jehoash king of Israel replied to Amaziah king of Judah: “A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son in marriage.’ Then a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח יוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל אֲמַצְיָ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ הַח֜וֹחַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֗וֹן שָׁ֠לַח אֶל הָאֶ֜רֶז אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּלְּבָנוֹן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנָֽה אֶת בִּתְּךָ֥ לִבְנִ֖י לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַֽתַּעֲבֹ֞ר חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן וַתִּרְמֹ֖ס אֶת הַחֽוֹחַ

verses.restored: You say, “You have struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you up to boast; now stay at home. Why should you be meddlesome to your hurt, that you and Judah should fall?”

familiar.text: Thou sayest, Lo, thou hast smitten the Edomites; and thine heart lifteth thee up to boast: abide now at home; why shouldest thou meddle to thine hurt, that thou shouldest fall, even thou, and Judah with thee?

modern.text: You have said, ‘Look, I have defeated Edom,’ and your heart has become proud and boastful. Now stay at home. Why should you stir up trouble so that you fall—you and Judah with you?”

original.text: אָמַ֗רְתָּ הִנֵּ֤ה הִכִּ֨יתָ֙ אֶת אֱד֔וֹם וּנְשָׂאֲךָ֥ לִבְּךָ֖ לְהַכְבִּ֑יד עַתָּה֙ שְׁבָ֣ה בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ לָ֤מָּה תִתְגָּרֶה֙ בְּרָעָ֔ה וְנָ֣פַלְתָּ֔ אַתָּ֖ה וִיהוּדָ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: But Amaziah would not hear; for it was from God that it should come to pass, to give them into the hand of their enemies, because they sought after the gods of Edom.

familiar.text: But Amaziah would not hear; for it came of God, that he might deliver them into the hand of their enemies, because they sought after the gods of Edom.

modern.text: But Amaziah would not listen, for this had come from God in order to deliver them into the hand of Jehoash, because they had sought the gods of Edom.

original.text: וְלֹא שָׁמַ֣ע אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ כִּ֤י מֵהָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ הִ֔יא לְמַ֖עַן תִּתָּ֣ם בְּיָ֑ד כִּ֣י דָֽרְשׁ֔וּ אֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֱדֽוֹם

verses.restored: So Joash king of Israel went up; they met face to face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh which belongs to Judah.

familiar.text: So Joash the king of Israel went up; and they saw one another in the face, both he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Bethshemesh, which belongeth to Judah.

modern.text: So Jehoash king of Israel advanced, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh in Judah.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַל יוֹאָ֤שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיִּתְרָא֣וּ פָנִ֔ים ה֖וּא וַאֲמַצְיָ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה בְּבֵ֥ית שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִיהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Judah was put to the worse before Israel, and they fled every man to his tent.

familiar.text: And Judah was put to the worse before Israel, and they fled every man to his tent.

modern.text: And Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his own home.

original.text: וַיִּנָּ֥גֶף יְהוּדָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָֽיו

verses.restored: And Joash king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh and brought him to Jerusalem; he broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits.

familiar.text: And Joash the king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, at Bethshemesh, and brought him to Jerusalem, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits.

modern.text: There at Beth-shemesh, Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz. Then Jehoash brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate—a section of four hundred cubits.

original.text: וְאֵת֩ אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֜ה בֶּן יוֹאָ֣שׁ בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֗ז תָּפַ֛שׂ יוֹאָ֥שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּבֵ֣ית שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וַיְבִיאֵ֨הוּ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיִּפְרֹ֞ץ בְּחוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם מִשַּׁ֤עַר אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד שַׁ֣עַר הַפּוֹנֶ֔ה אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אַמָּֽה

verses.restored: He took all the gold and silver and all the vessels that were found in the house of God with Obed‑edom, and the treasures of the king's house and the hostages, and returned to Samaria.

familiar.text: And he took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of God with Obededom, and the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria.

modern.text: He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of God with Obed-edom and in the treasuries of the royal palace, as well as some hostages. Then he returned to Samaria. The Death of Amaziah (2 Kings 14:17–20)

original.text: וְכָֽל הַזָּהָ֣ב וְהַכֶּ֡סֶף וְאֵ֣ת כָּל הַ֠כֵּלִים הַנִּמְצְאִ֨ים בְּבֵית הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים עִם עֹבֵ֣ד אֱד֗וֹם וְאֶת אֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י הַתַּֽעֲרֻב֑וֹת וַיָּ֖שָׁב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

familiar.text: And Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years.

modern.text: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

original.text: וַיְחִ֨י אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ בֶן יוֹאָשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֣י מ֔וֹת יוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חֲמֵ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, first and last, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, first and last, behold, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from beginning to end, are they not written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel?

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הֲלֹא֙ הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵי יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Now when Amaziah turned away from following YHWH, they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem; he fled to Lachish, but they sent to Lachish and killed him there.

familiar.text: Now after the time that Amaziah did turn away from following the LORD they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem; and he fled to Lachish: but they sent to Lachish after him, and slew him there.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Verse reflects witness conflations in the MT and other traditions; see source_tail for variant lines.

modern.text: From the time that Amaziah turned from following the LORD, a conspiracy was formed against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But men were sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.

original.text: וּמֵעֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁר סָ֤ר אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּקְשְׁר֨וּ עָלָ֥יו קֶ֛שֶׁר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיָּ֣נָס לָכִ֑ישָׁה וַיִּשְׁלְח֤וּ אַחֲרָיו֙ לָכִ֔ישָׁה וַיְמִיתֻ֖הוּ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: They brought him on horses, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.

familiar.text: And they brought him upon horses, and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.

modern.text: They carried him back on horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of Judah.

original.text: וַיִּשָּׂאֻ֖הוּ עַל הַסּוּסִ֑ים וַֽיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ עִם אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֥יר יְהוּדָֽה

translation_notes: Rendered יהוה as YHWH throughout; other divine titles (אֱלֹהִים, בֵּית־הָאֱלֹהִים) left as God / house of God per source wording.
Preserves the Torah quotation (Deut./Moses) and the prophet's rebuke; military numbers taken from the Masoretic consonantal text without emendation.
Verse 27 presents conflated/parenthetical readings in the witnesses (see source_tail); requires later witness-critical annotation.
safety_note: Contains violence, executions, forced deaths, and idol worship; intended for scholarly use and not advocacy.
